doc.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Volkswagen commercial and Black jingle musicians
summary: Ten musicians get out of a Volkswagen; Everett Barksdale and other Black players in the jingle business.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: One commercial that I read about – maybe you can enlighten me on – was the Volkswagen commercial.
Tell me that story, particularly the part about Everett Barksdale.

Oh yeah. We had a thing for – a jingle for Volkswagen. Ten of us got out of a Volkswagen playing When the Saints go marching in, something like that. Snooky was driving the Volkswagen. It just drove like “Vrrrrrrrrr” and stopped, and we got out, and everybody’s playing. It was just to show how amazingly this area was. Ten cats could get out with instruments and playing. Everett Barksdale was one of the people who was on the gig. I was the contractor at the time, and Barksdale and I – after a while, there were several black musicians involved in jingles.
I’ve got a list here: Milt Hinton, Jimmy Nottingham, Joe Wilder, Ernie Royal, Jerome Richardson, Thad Jones, Joe Newman, Hank Jones, George Duvivier.

Everett Barksdale was one. He was a guitar player. Wally Richardson was another one. He was a guitar player. The guitar players were on every kind of date there was. Aside from the four or five caucasians, who were always extremely busy, they needed more, so that opened the door for a few of the black qualified people who could do it. There were a few more, but not a hell of a lot more than what you have already named.
